subject.title: fix(sessions): prevent lifecycle races and unsafe session management

question: Should plugin runtimes be permanently restricted to sessions whose persisted `pluginOwnerId` exactly matches their runtime owner, even when older callers may have relied on cross-owner patch, reset, delete, fork, link, or adoption behavior?
rationale: The code, tests, and real behavior proof establish that the new rule works, but only maintainers can choose whether this intentional compatibility break is the permanent plugin/session security contract.

options.title: Accept authoritative plugin ownership
options.body: Merge with the new same-owner fail-closed rule and treat cross-owner session operations as unsupported going forward.

options.title: Preserve selected legacy operations
options.body: Pause the PR and specify narrowly which cross-owner operation, if any, remains supported and under what authorization contract.

options.title: Split the broader tool additions
options.body: Keep the ownership hardening in a narrower PR and review model-visible reset/delete and timeout additions separately.

recommendation.title: Accept authoritative plugin ownership
recommendation.body: Merge with the new same-owner fail-closed rule and treat cross-owner session operations as unsupported going forward.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor directly to the session lifecycle implementation and its compatibility rationale.
